description: Kick drum voice: a sine oscillator with a swept pitch envelope, self phase modulation, a four-pole low-pass, a saturator and an accent input, and a WAV file that can be loaded to modulate it

params.text: Sets the pitch the sweep settles to, 20Hz to 200Hz
Sets how far above that pitch each hit starts, 0Hz to 500Hz
Sets how quickly the pitch falls back, 0.5 to 4; at 0.5 the fall takes 30ms and at 4 it takes under 4ms
Sets how long the hit takes to die away, 10ms to 1000ms
Drives the filtered signal into a saturator, 0 to 10, leaving it alone at zero and pushing it six times over at the top
Sets how deeply the loaded sample modulates the oscillator, 0 to 10; with no sample loaded it does nothing
Feeds the oscillator's own last two outputs back into its phase, 0 to 1, taking the sine towards a harder, brassier tone
Sets the corner of the four-pole low-pass after the oscillator, 40Hz at the bottom of its travel to 20000Hz at the top
Cycles the way the loaded sample acts on the oscillator: PM for phase modulation, RM for ring modulation, AM for amplitude modulation, SYNC for a phase reset at the sample's zero crossings

inputs.text: A rising edge through 2V fires the kick and samples the accent jack
Multiplies the pitch of the oscillator, one volt per octave, on top of the PITCH knob
Added to the SWEEP knob, 50Hz per volt; the total is held between 0Hz and 1000Hz
Added to the BEND knob, 0.35 per volt; the total is held between 0.5 and 4
Added to the DECAY knob, 100ms per volt; the total is held between 10ms and 2000ms
Added to the DRIVE knob, one unit of its ten per volt; the total is held between the two ends of it
Added to the FEEDBACK knob, a tenth per volt; the total is held between 0 and 1
Added to the TONE knob, one unit of its ten per volt; the total is held between the two ends of it
Added to the sample modulation knob, one unit of its ten per volt; the total is held between the two ends of it
Read once at each trigger: 0V gives the quiet hit, 10V raises the level by 6dB, the pitch sweep by four fifths and the drive by 2dB, and anything between scales all three

notes: the sample controls do nothing until a WAV file is loaded. Click the small strip under the title to open a file dialog; right-click it for Clear Sample.
the mode lamp stays dark and the mode button refuses to move while no sample is loaded.
the CV jacks here are scaled for ±5V; the knob-and-jack totals are then clamped, several of them to a wider span than the knob alone can reach.
the loaded file is read into a 2048-point table and played back at the oscillator's own frequency, so it acts as a waveform rather than as a sample with a length of its own.
menu: 2x Oversample — runs the voice at twice the sample rate and filters it back down, which softens the aliasing the saturator makes on high sweeps
